# pdfnative-react

> A declarative React renderer for the zero-dependency `pdfnative` PDF engine.
> JSX compiles, via a custom React reconciler, into a `pdfnative` DocumentParams
> object and renders real PDF bytes — no DOM, no headless browser, no native
> modules. It is a declarative block flow, not a CSS/flexbox layout engine.

Version: 1.3.0 · pairs with pdfnative 1.8.0. Current release: 1.3.0.
Verified on 2026-09-22 against the source tree.

This file is an LLM-facing capability summary. For the machine-readable JSON
version, call `capabilityManifest()`; for schemas, call `schema(subject)`.

## Install

```
npm install pdfnative-react pdfnative react
```

Requires React 19, pdfnative >= 1.8, Node.js >= 22.

## Core idea

JSX components map 1:1 onto pdfnative blocks. A custom react-reconciler compiles
the tree synchronously (no DOM) into `DocumentParams`, which `pdfnative` renders
to a `Uint8Array` PDF. 19 components, 14 block kinds, 18 DocSpec fields,
37 lint rules, 6 error codes, 27 Unicode scripts.

## Components

- Document (root: title, footerText, metadata, fontEntries, layout, outline, pageLabels, watermark, header, footer, attachments, tagged, print, pdfx, outputIntent, typography, creationDate)
- Page (explicit page boundary; auto-pagination otherwise)
- Section (sugar: title + grouped content; level?, color?, break?)
- Heading (level 1-3; keepWithNext?)
- Paragraph / Text (alias) (fontSize?, lineHeight?, align?: 'left'|'center'|'right'|'justify', indent?, color?, keepWithNext?, splittable?)
- List (ordered?) + Item (items may nest sub-lists: child <List>, nested <Item>, or items={{text,items}})
- Table + Row (header?, variant, pointed) + Cell  — or pass headers/rows props; cellBorders?, cellVAlign?, zebra?
- Image (data: Uint8Array)
- Link (url | href)
- Spacer (height)
- PageBreak
- TableOfContents / Toc (alias)
- Barcode (format, data) — qr, code128, ean13, pdf417, datamatrix
- Svg (data: path or markup; <text>/<tspan> render as selectable PDF text)
- Chart (chartType, series) — bar, barH, line, pie, donut, stackedBar, stackedBarH,
  area, scatter; log/time scales (axis.scale, xAxis), secondary right axis (axis2 +
  series yAxis:'right'), per-point dataLabels, labelStride/labelRotation; series
  xValues required for scatter/positional axes. Native vector, PDF/A-safe.
- FormField (fieldType, name) — interactive AcroForm widgets

Colour (every `color`, chart colors/series color, cellBorders.color, zebra,
watermark, header/footer color, layout.colors): '#rrggbb' | [r,g,b] (0-255) |
'r g b' (0-1) | [c,m,y,k] (percent, 0-100) | 'c m y k' (0-1). Three values are
DeviceRGB, four are DeviceCMYK.

## Document-level page furniture (props on <Document>, not components)

- watermark: string | WatermarkOptions   (a string is shorthand for { text: { text } })
- header / footer: PageTemplate { left?, center?, right?, fontSize?, color? }
  Placeholders resolved at render time: {page} {pages} {date} {title}
  ({date} follows creationDate when pinned)
- attachments: PdfAttachment[] { filename, data, mimeType, description?, relationship? }
  Requires tagged: 'pdfa3b' — the engine throws otherwise.
- tagged: boolean | 'pdfa1b' | 'pdfa2b' | 'pdfa2u' | 'pdfa3b'
  PDF/A requires embedded fonts: pair with fontEntries.
- print: PrintOptions { bleed? | trimBox?/bleedBox?/artBox?/cropBox? ([llx,lly,urx,ury]),
  marks?: boolean | { crop?, registration?, colourBars?: boolean | { tints?, size? }, length?, offset?, weight? }, userUnit? (1-75000) }
  Print production (engine >= 1.7; colourBars >= 1.8). bleed and trimBox are mutually
  exclusive; marks need a TrimBox source; userUnit is rejected under 'pdfa1b';
  colour bars want a 5 mm (14.17 pt) bleed.
- pdfx: 'pdfx4'  — PDF/X-4 (ISO 15930-7). Needs outputIntent with a printer (prtr)
  ICC profile, metadata.trapped 'True'|'False', fontEntries; exclusive with tagged
  and layout.encryption; a TrimBox or an ArtBox per page, not both. Each constraint
  is an L_PDFX_* lint rule before it is an E_INPUT throw. Check bytes with the
  engine's validatePdfX() (not re-exported; docs/RECIPES.md).
- outputIntent: { iccProfile: Uint8Array (RGB/CMYK/Gray), outputConditionIdentifier, registryName?, outputCondition?, info? }
  Honoured under tagged, required under pdfx, ignored otherwise (lint warns).
  The profile must be a real ICC file (acsp signature, size field) — L_OUTPUT_INTENT_PROFILE.
  No press profile is bundled.
- typography: TypographyOptions — all opt-in; unset => byte-identical to earlier releases:
  splitParagraphs (boolean), orphans / widows (number >= 1, need splitParagraphs),
  keepHeadingsWithNext (boolean | { minLines }), unitBinding (boolean | { units }),
  bindShortWords (boolean | { words }), punctuationSpacing ('fr' | 'fr-CA' | [{ char, side, space }]),
  opticalMargins (boolean), metrics ('approximate' | 'exact'), fontFeatures (['tnum','pnum','lnum','onum','zero','ordn','sups','subs','smcp','c2sc','case']),
  kerning (boolean), hyphenationLanguage (BCP 47 tag for setHyphenationProvider).
  Limits: kerning, fontFeatures and the 'fr' narrow space need fontEntries (base-14 has none — 'fr' degrades to 'fr-CA');
  metrics 'exact' acts on base-14 text only; tnum/lnum are no-ops on Noto Sans (TYPOGRAPHY_FEATURE_INEFFECTIVE);
  no hyphenation dictionary ships (soft hyphens U+00AD are honoured). Lint: L_TYPOGRAPHY_INEFFECTIVE.
- creationDate: Date | ISO 8601 string — pins /CreationDate, /ModDate, XMP dates,
  the {date} placeholder and the trailer /ID; dates are always UTC (+00'00'), so a
  pinned document gives the same bytes on every host. An unparseable string is E_INPUT.
  Process-wide: setDefaultCreationDate(date | null). The library reads NO environment
  variable (not SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH). Not reproducible by design: layout.encryption.

All ten fold into `layout` under the engine's keys (watermark, headerTemplate,
footerTemplate, attachments, tagged, print, pdfx, outputIntent, typography,
creationDate). An explicit `layout` prop wins (replaces whole, no deep merge).
Document.outline: OutlineItem[] | 'auto'. Document.pageLabels: PageLabelRange[].
metadata.trapped: 'True' | 'False' | 'Unknown' (prepress /Trapped + XMP; PDF/X needs a known state).
layout.viewerPreferences also takes duplex, pickTrayByPDFSize,
printPageRange ([[first,last], ...] 1-based) and numCopies.
layout.strict (boolean, JSON-safe) escalates the engine's 9 diagnostic codes to
thrown errors; layout.onDiagnostic (function — not representable in JSON specs)
receives them instead of the default console.warn:
PDFA_NO_FONT_ENTRIES, PDFA_UNEMBEDDED_FORM_FONT, PDFA_DEVICE_CMYK_IMAGE,
PDFA_DEVICE_CMYK_CONTENT, PDFA_ICC_PROFILE_VERSION, PDFX_NO_FONT_ENTRIES,
PDFX_DEVICE_CMYK, PDFX_ANNOTATIONS, TYPOGRAPHY_FEATURE_INEFFECTIVE.

## Rendering

- renderToBytes(node, options?) -> Uint8Array
- renderToBlob(node, options?) -> Blob (application/pdf)
- renderToStream(node, options?) -> AsyncGenerator<Uint8Array> (constant memory)
  Streaming cannot include ['toc'] blocks or {pages} in header/footer templates
  (the final page count is unknown when page 1 is emitted). renderToStream
  validates this EAGERLY and throws at call time; use the buffered entries
  (renderToBytes / renderToResponse with buffered: true) for those documents.
- renderToResponse(node, options?) -> Promise<Response>  (web standard; streams by default)
- renderToFile(node, path, options?) -> Promise<void> (Node only)
- renderToFileStream(node, path, options?) -> Promise<StreamToFileResult> (Node, constant memory)
- compileDocument(node) -> DocumentParams (inspect the model)
- inspectDocument(node, options?) -> LayoutInspection (page/block geometry, no render)
- lintDocument(node, options?) -> LintReport (accessibility + engine constraints)

`options`: { layout?: Partial<PdfLayoutOptions>, fontEntries?: FontEntry[], fonts?: FontsMap }.
`renderToResponse` also takes { fileName?, disposition?: 'inline'|'attachment',
buffered?, status?, cacheControl?, etag? (string verbatim | true = derive from
bytes, implies buffering; stable across hosts only when creationDate is pinned),
headers? }. fonts (loader map) is honored only by async entries (renderToFile,
renderToFileStream, renderToResponse, usePdf, usePdfStream); for sync entries
do `fontEntries: await resolveFonts({...})`.

## Fonts & assets

- resolveFonts(map) -> Promise<FontEntry[]>  (map: { lang: () => import('pdfnative/fonts/…-data.js') })
  27 Unicode scripts are bundled by the engine as font modules; 1.8.0 added
  lo (Lao), nod (Tai Tham), khb (New Tai Lue), tdd (Tai Le), cjm (Cham), and
  ha/yo/ig/sw (Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Swahili) as aliases of the latin module.
- validateFontData(data) -> FontValidationResult { valid, errors, warnings }  (opt-in font check)
- fromUrl(url, init?) -> Promise<Uint8Array>  (image bytes)
- fromBase64(payload) -> Uint8Array           (base64 or data: URI)

## Hooks & client components (browser only)

Import these from the `pdfnative-react/client` subpath, which ships with the
'use client' directive applied. The root barrel exports them too, for apps with
no RSC boundary.

    import { PDFViewer, usePdf } from 'pdfnative-react/client';

IMPORTANT — the RSC boundary: this package drives a React reconciler and needs
createContext, which React's 'react-server' condition does not provide. Importing
it from a Server Component or a 'use server' file fails at module load. Use a
Route Handler (app/**/route.ts) instead — that is what renderToResponse is for.

- usePdf(element, options?) -> { url, blob, bytes, loading, error, update }
- usePdfStream(element, options?) -> { getStream() }
- PDFViewer({ document, options?, className?, style?, width?, height?, title? }) — live iframe preview
- PDFDownloadLink({ document, fileName?, options?, children }) — anchor download
- BlobProvider({ document, options?, children: (state) => ReactNode })

## Font / environment helpers (re-exported from pdfnative)

registerFonts, registerFont, loadFontData, downloadBlob, initNodeCompression,
setDeflateImpl (a zlib-wrapped DEFLATE implementation so layout.compress produces
real compression in browsers/workers; rejects raw DEFLATE since engine 1.8.0),
setDeflateRawImpl (a RAW deflate function; the engine adds the zlib framing),
wrapZlib (wrap a raw deflater by hand), setDefaultCreationDate /
getDefaultCreationDate (process-wide creation instant; null restores the clock),
setHyphenationProvider / getHyphenationProvider ((word, lang?) => break offsets).
Every one is the engine's own function, re-exported unchanged.

## Compact agent authoring (token-frugal DocSpec)

For LLM agents: a compact, JSON-serializable grammar that compiles to the SAME
PDF as the equivalent JSX (built on the same components, so they cannot drift).
Prefer it when generating documents programmatically.

- compileSpec(spec) -> DocumentParams
- specToElement(spec) -> ReactElement (<Document> tree)
- renderSpecToBytes / renderSpecToBlob / renderSpecToStream / renderSpecToFile
- renderSpecToFileStream / renderSpecToResponse
- inspectSpec(spec, options?) -> LayoutInspection
- lintSpec(spec, options?) -> LintReport
- validateSpec(spec: unknown) -> { ok, errors, warnings }   (no JSON-Schema engine needed)

DocSpec fields (18): title, footerText, metadata, fontEntries, layout, outline,
pageLabels, watermark, header, footer, attachments, tagged, print, pdfx,
outputIntent, typography, creationDate (ISO string), blocks — every one optional
but blocks.
Block tuples (kind, ...payload, opts?):
- ['h1'|'h2'|'h3', text, opts?]   opts: color?, keepWithNext?
- ['p', text, opts?]   opts: fontSize?, lineHeight?, align? (incl. 'justify'), indent?, color?, keepWithNext?, splittable?
- ['ul'|'ol', items, opts?]   items entry = string | { text, items }  (nested sub-lists)
- ['table', { h?, r, columns?, zebra?, caption?, cellBorders?, cellVAlign?, ... }]   r row = string[] | PdfRow
- ['img', { data, ... }]
- ['link', text, { url, ... }]
- ['sp', height?]
- ['br']
- ['page', blocks]
- ['toc', opts?]
- ['qr'|'code128'|'ean13'|'pdf417'|'datamatrix', data, opts?]
- ['svg', data, opts?]
- ['chart', { chartType, series, categories?, title?, width?, height?, legend?, axis?, axis2?, xAxis?, dataLabels?, labelStride?, labelRotation?, markers?, colors?, align?, altText? }]
- ['field', { fieldType, name, ... }]

## Agent surface

- doctor() -> { ok, checks: [{ name, status: 'ok'|'warn'|'error', value, detail }] }
  Environment pre-flight. NEVER throws, including when the pdfnative peer is
  missing. Engine probe newest-first: a 1.7.x engine is reported as needing >= 1.8.0.
  Call this first in an unfamiliar environment.
- capabilityManifest() -> everything the package can do, as plain JSON:
  components, specBlocks (the whole grammar), specFields, entrypoints, errorCodes,
  lintRules, schemaSubjects, and the contract invariants (engine '^1.8.0').
- schema(subject?) -> Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema; schemaId(subject?) -> versioned $id.
  Subjects: doc-spec (default), render-options, lint-report, spec-validation,
  doctor, manifest, list. The $id embeds the package version, so a caching
  consumer can detect contract drift. Unknown subject throws E_INPUT.
  docSpecSchema() / docSpecSchemaId() are retained and delegate to 'doc-spec'.
- aiGovernancePolicy(), agentRulesText(), validateIssueDraft(md) — the
  human-in-the-loop contract, shipped as runtime capability.

Recommended loop:
  doctor -> capabilityManifest -> schema -> validateSpec -> compileSpec -> lintSpec -> render

Four dry-run tiers, cheapest first:
  1. validateSpec(unknown)  malformed shape (V_* codes, path-anchored)
  2. compileSpec(spec)      structure that cannot map onto the model
  3. lintSpec(spec)         accessibility + engine constraints (L_* codes)
  4. inspectSpec(spec)      pagination and geometry (costs ~a render)

Tier 5 — verify the RENDERED output (post-render):
  - extractText (engine, on the bytes): did text really render, or .notdef?
    Honours /ActualText since engine 1.8.0 (shaped scripts extract as source text).
  - validatePdfUA (engine) / veraPDF: is the PDF/A or PDF/UA claim true?
    The repo itself gates on veraPDF: `npm run validate:pdfa` renders a
    PDF/A corpus (both authoring doors, 2 negative canaries) and validates
    it with the pinned reference validator; blocking in CI.
  - validatePdfX (engine): is the PDF/X-4 claim structurally true? Not a
    certified preflight. `npm run validate:pdfx` runs it over the repo's corpus.
  - VISION AGENTS: rasterize with a standard external tool and LOOK at it —
    `pdftoppm -png -r 144 out.pdf page` (poppler) or
    `mutool draw -o page-%d.png -r 144 out.pdf` (mupdf). Judge the PNG
    against your intent (layout, chart shape, clipping). No rasterizer is
    bundled (no new dependency, ever). Runnable with graceful degradation:
    samples/agent/visual-verify.tsx · recipe: docs/RECIPES.md.

Reproducible output for agents: set creationDate in the spec (ISO string) and
compare bytes across runs; the same spec gives the same SHA-256 on any host.

## Errors

Every error carries a stable code. Branch on the code, never the message.

- PdfReactError (base) — .code, .toJSON() -> { ok: false, error: { code, message } }
  Accepts ES2022 ErrorOptions: new PdfReactError(msg, code, { cause }); the
  envelope deliberately omits the cause.
- PdfStructureError extends PdfReactError — code 'E_STRUCTURE'
- toErrorEnvelope(unknown) -> the same envelope for any thrown value; an engine
  input error (PDF/X coherence, print geometry, output intent, chart) is E_INPUT.
- ErrorCode: E_STRUCTURE, E_INPUT, E_UNSUPPORTED, E_ENV, E_POLICY, E_RUNTIME

## Lint rules (stable L_* codes)

37 lint rules — 23 error, 13 warning, 1 info.

errors:   L_EMPTY_DOCUMENT, L_TAGGED_NO_FONTS, L_TAGGED_ENCRYPTED,
          L_ATTACHMENTS_NEED_PDFA3, L_MAX_BLOCKS_EXCEEDED, L_CHART_EMPTY,
          L_CHART_SERIES, L_CHART_CATEGORIES, L_CHART_VALUES, L_CHART_POINTS,
          L_CHART_LOG_SCALE, L_CHART_X_AXIS, L_CHART_LABELS, L_PRINT_BOXES,
          L_VIEWER_PRINT_RANGE, L_OUTPUT_INTENT_PROFILE, L_PDFX_TARGET,
          L_PDFX_TAGGED_CONFLICT, L_PDFX_ENCRYPTED, L_PDFX_OUTPUT_INTENT,
          L_PDFX_TRAPPED_UNKNOWN, L_PDFX_BOXES, L_PDFX_NO_FONTS
warnings: L_IMAGE_ALT, L_TABLE_HEADERS, L_HEADING_HIERARCHY, L_FIELD_LABEL,
          L_LINK_TEXT, L_MAX_BLOCKS, L_OUTPUT_INTENT_IGNORED,
          L_TAGGED_FORM_FONTS, L_OVERFLOW, L_PDFX_ANNOTATIONS,
          L_TYPOGRAPHY_INEFFECTIVE, L_PRINT_COLOUR_BARS, L_CMYK_INTENT_MISMATCH
info:     L_CHART_ALT

TWENTY of them pre-empt an exception the engine raises at build time: the eight
L_CHART_* errors, L_PRINT_BOXES (delegates to the engine's own
validatePrintOptions, so its message is the engine's), L_VIEWER_PRINT_RANGE,
L_ATTACHMENTS_NEED_PDFA3, L_TAGGED_ENCRYPTED, L_MAX_BLOCKS_EXCEEDED,
L_OUTPUT_INTENT_PROFILE and the six PDF/X coherence rules (their message is the
engine's message). Five mirror an engine diagnostic that throws under
layout.strict. L_MAX_BLOCKS_EXCEEDED fires against the engine default of
100 000 blocks even when layout.maxBlocks is unset. L_OVERFLOW requires
{ overflow: true }. A 1.2.0 document trips none of the twelve 1.3.0 rules.

## Notes

- No `<View>` / flexbox by design — pdfnative is a declarative block flow.
- React 19 only (single react-reconciler version contract); React 18 is not planned.
- Authoring only. For byte-level post-processing (merge/split, form fill/flatten,
  text extraction, decryption, annotations, signing, PDF/X or PDF/UA validation,
  font compilation) use the pdfnative engine directly on the bytes this library
  produces — see docs/RECIPES.md.
- No outbound network calls, no telemetry, no autonomous GitHub writes, no
  environment variables read.
